subject: design-technology
title: Applications: CNC, 3D Printing and Laser Cutting
welcome_lead: Tour the workshop and see CNC routers, 3D printers and laser cutters turning files into finished parts.
meta_desc: Apply CNC, 3D printing and laser cutting in real GCSE Design & Technology projects.
final_note: You can match a CAM process to a material and design brief.

concepts.def: Computer-controlled cutter for wood and plastic sheet.
Fused deposition modelling 3D printing with filament.
Burning or vaporising sheet material with a laser.
Knife-cutting sticky vinyl for signs and stickers.

walkthroughs.body_html: CNC routers remove material with a spinning bit and suit MDF, plywood and acrylic. CNC milling works on metal billets. Both are subtractive — they cut away from a block — so they produce waste chips that can be recycled.

FDM printers melt PLA or ABS filament layer by layer. SLA printers cure liquid resin with UV light, giving smoother finish and finer detail. Both are additive, so only the part itself is built — there is much less waste.

A clear acrylic sign with sharp lettering is best cut on a laser cutter because it leaves a flame-polished edge. A complex curved phone stand suits FDM 3D printing. A vinyl logo for a shop window calls for a vinyl cutter.
